relationships.statement: \mathfrak{so}(4)\cong\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: Identify so(4) with bivectors in oriented Euclidean four-space. The self-dual and anti-self-dual bivectors are commuting three-dimensional ideals, each isomorphic to so(3), hence to su(2).

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{so}(4,\mathbb C)\cong\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)\oplus\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: Complexify the compact so(4) decomposition and the real form su(2).

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{so}(2,2)\cong\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R)\oplus\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: The action (X,Y)·A=XA−AY on real 2-by-2 matrices preserves determinant, a form of signature (2,2). Its infinitesimal kernel is zero: XA=AY for every A forces X=Y scalar, and trace zero then forces both to vanish. Both algebras have dimension six.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{su}(2)\cong\mathfrak{sp}(1)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: Identify imaginary quaternions with trace-zero skew-Hermitian 2-by-2 matrices; quaternion multiplication is represented by matrix multiplication.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{su}(2)\cong\mathfrak{so}(3)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: The adjoint action on the three-dimensional imaginary-quaternion space preserves its Euclidean norm, is faithful infinitesimally, and both algebras have dimension three.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{sp}(2)\cong\mathfrak{so}(5)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: Act by X·A=XA−AX on traceless Hermitian quaternionic 2-by-2 matrices. This five-dimensional real space has positive form tr(A²); the infinitesimal action is injective, and source and target both have dimension ten.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{su}(4)\cong\mathfrak{so}(6)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: The exterior-square representation preserves the symmetric wedge pairing on Λ²C⁴. Its compatible antilinear Hodge involution has a six-dimensional real fixed space; the differentiated action is faithful and both algebras have dimension fifteen.

conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: For a 2-by-2 matrix X, XᵀJ+JX=(tr X)J.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)\cong\mathfrak{so}(3,\mathbb C)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: The adjoint action preserves the nondegenerate Killing form; its kernel is the zero center, and both algebras have dimension three.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R)\cong\mathfrak{so}(2,1)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: The form tr(X²) on trace-zero real 2-by-2 matrices has signature (2,1). Its adjoint action is injective and dimension three.

relationships.statement: \mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)_{\mathbb R}\cong\mathfrak{so}(3,1)
conditions: Scalar field and any restriction of scalars are exactly as shown.

evidence.method: The action X·H=XH+HX* on Hermitian 2-by-2 complex matrices infinitesimally preserves determinant, a quadratic form of signature (1,3). If this action vanishes then X is skew-Hermitian and commutes with every Hermitian matrix, hence is scalar; trace zero forces X=0. Both algebras have real dimension six, and changing the sign of the form does not change its orthogonal Lie algebra.
